Decision: split into 9 children (decomposition attempt 3). The supplied 17-step proof combines five different kinds of mathematics: (1) differential topology of the C¹ graph (steps 1, 3, 5, 6); (2) Hausdorff-measure bounds (step 8); (3) orientation and Jacobian linear algebra (steps 3, 7); (4) identification of the IMRep's approximate tangent planes and orientation, giving an integer density (steps 9–12); (5) the boundary test and distributional constancy (steps 13–14). None is a single library result, and together they are far too large for one Lean theorem.

The split is shaped by one constraint. In this run every childless node is a machine leaf (leaf_lean_agent_review = false). A leaf candidate may only append one theorem to the frozen GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean, with no import or helper (leaf_verification.check_source_delta). Parents may edit Submission freely (parent_verification.check_parent_git_delta). Two library results the proof needs are outside Submission's import closure (checked by name-existence tests):
- the nonlinear area formula Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative, with areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp (modules WeightedArea and Area);
- the constancy theorem Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero (module DistributionalConstancy).

So this node's own (parent) proof applies these two results. It adds `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WeightedArea` and `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter08.DistributionalConstancy`; with these imports all 103 frozen GMT.Ch07 declarations stay hash-identical. Every child is stated so that it is provable inside the frozen closure.

This also fixes a latent defect in the never-consumed attempts v1/v2. There, the orientation child contained the integral area identity and the constancy child applied Chapter08; both were leaves and could not add those imports. v1/v2 passed audit but were silently dropped because the earlier worker had max_nodes = 200 and the DAG was full. 5. BT (using u(D) ⊆ B_h(0) from step 1) gives ∫_D G·∂ⱼa = 0 for every smooth compactly supported a in D. SC extends this to C¹ tests, in the exact hypothesis form of ae_eq_const_of_weak_coordinate_derivatives_zero. D is open and convex (hence preconnected) and G ∈ L¹_loc(D), so G = c a.e. on D. As Lⁿ(D) > 0 and G ∈ ℤ a.e., c = m ∈ ℤ.
6. For tsupport ω ⊆ C: T(ω) = ∫_D G·ω(Φ)(b) = m·∫_D ω(Φ)(b) = m·∫_Σ ξ(ω) dHⁿ (step 4 with f ≡ 1).
7. m ≠ 0. Otherwise T vanishes on test forms supported in B_ρ(z), whose closure B̄_ρ(z) is compact and contained in U. Then z ∈ T.zeroRegion, contradicting z ∈ T.support.
8. The witnesses of z ∈ regularSet T are ρ, m, Σ and ξ:
   - ball z ρ ⊆ U and z ∈ Σ;
   - GE and IsOrientation n Σ ξ;
   - for compact K ⊆ ball z ρ, Σ ∩ K ⊆ Φ(B̄_ρ(0)) by step 1, which has finite measure by MB(ii) since ρ < s;

subproblems.title: Orthogonal isometric embeddings of complementary dimensions give orthogonal coordinates on ℝ^{n+k}
subproblems.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ and let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} be linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v ∈ ℝⁿ, w ∈ ℝ^k. Then (a) every x ∈ ℝ^{n+k} can be written as x = ιv + ι'w with v ∈ ℝⁿ and w ∈ ℝ^k, and (b) ‖ιv + ι'w‖² = ‖v‖² + ‖w‖² for all v ∈ ℝⁿ and w ∈ ℝ^k.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (ι : Euclid n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)), (∀ v w, inner ℝ (ι v) (ι' w) = 0) → (∀ x : Euclid (n + k), ∃ v : Euclid n, ∃ w : Euclid k, x = ι v + ι' w) ∧ ∀ (v : Euclid n) (w : Euclid k), ‖ι v + ι' w‖ ^ 2 = ‖v‖ ^ 2 + ‖w‖ ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof ("the ranges L := ι(ℝⁿ) and L' := ι'(ℝ^k) are orthogonal subspaces of dimensions n and k, so ℝ^{n+k} = L ⊕ L'", and "x = z + ιPr(x) + ι'Q(x) and |x − z|² = |Pr x|² + |Q x|²"). It is extracted as a lemma because these orthogonal coordinates are used by two siblings (openness of the cylinder C, compactness of the support of the boundary test form) and by the parent assembly (B̄_ρ(z) ⊆ C, uniqueness of graph coordinates, ‖v‖ ≤ ‖Φ(v) − z‖).
Notation: ℝ^m means Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product (inner ℝ).
Formalization note: unless this child is split further it is a machine leaf (one theorem appended to the frozen GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean, no new import or helper declaration); all lemmas cited are in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission.
1. Part (b). Let v ∈ ℝⁿ and w ∈ ℝ^k. By the expansion of the square of the norm of a sum in a real inner product space (norm_add_sq_real), ‖ιv + ι'w‖² = ‖ιv‖² + 2⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ + ‖ι'w‖². Linear isometries preserve norms (LinearIsometry.norm_map), so ‖ιv‖ = ‖v‖ and ‖ι'w‖ = ‖w‖, and ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 by hypothesis. Hence ‖ιv + ι'w‖² = ‖v‖² + ‖w‖².
2. Let L := range ι and L' := range ι' (LinearMap.range of the underlying linear maps, submodules of ℝ^{n+k}). A linear isometry is injective (LinearIsometry.injective), so dim L = dim ℝⁿ = n and dim L' = dim ℝ^k = k (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj and finrank_euclideanSpace_fin).
3. L ⊓ L' = ⊥. Let y ∈ L ∩ L' and write y = ιv = ι'w. Then ‖y‖² = ⟨y, y⟩ = ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 (real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq), so y = 0.
4. By the dimension formula dim(L ⊔ L') + dim(L ⊓ L') = dim L + dim L' (Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq) and step 3 (finrank of ⊥ is 0, finrank_bot), dim(L ⊔ L') = n + k = dim ℝ^{n+k} (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). A subspace of full dimension is the whole space (Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq), so L ⊔ L' = ⊤.
5. Part (a). Let x ∈ ℝ^{n+k}. Then x ∈ ⊤ = L ⊔ L', so by Submodule.mem_sup there are y ∈ L and y' ∈ L' with y + y' = x. Writing y = ιv (v ∈ ℝⁿ) and y' = ι'w (w ∈ ℝ^k) (LinearMap.mem_range) gives x = ιv + ι'w.
Steps 1 and 5 are the two conjuncts of the statement. (For n = 0 or k = 0 the same argument applies verbatim: the corresponding range is {0}.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Pythagoras: ‖ιv + ι'w‖² = ‖ιv‖² + 2⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ + ‖ι'w‖² = ‖v‖² + ‖w‖² (isometries, orthogonality).
range ι and range ι' have dimensions n and k (injective isometries) and meet only in 0 (orthogonality).
Dimension formula: dim(range ι ⊔ range ι') = n + k, so range ι ⊔ range ι' = ⊤.
Submodule.mem_sup decomposes every x as ιv + ι'w.

subproblems.title: A C¹ graph over a ball is an injectively parametrized embedded C¹ submanifold with tangent spaces range DΦ
subproblems.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, let ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} be linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, let s > 0, z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, and let u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k be of class C¹ on the open ball D = B_s(0). Put Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v) and Σ := Φ(D). Then (i) Φ is injective on D; (ii) for every v ∈ D, Φ is differentiable at v and fderiv ℝ Φ v is injective; (iii) Σ is an embedded n-dimensional C¹ submanifold in the sense of the contract (IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n Σ); (iv) for every v ∈ D, the contract's tangent space tangentSpace Σ (Φ(v)) equals the range of fderiv ℝ Φ v (as a set).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n k : ℕ) (ι : Euclid n →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) (u : Euclid n → Euclid k) (z : Euclid (n + k)) (s : ℝ), (∀ v w, inner ℝ (ι v) (ι' w) = 0) → 0 < s → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u (ball 0 s) → InjOn (fun v => z + ι v + ι' (u v)) (ball (0 : Euclid n) s) ∧ (∀ v ∈ ball (0 : Euclid n) s, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun v => z + ι v + ι' (u v)) v ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ (fun v => z + ι v + ι' (u v)) v)) ∧ IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n ((fun v => z + ι v + ι' (u v)) '' ball (0 : Euclid n) s) ∧ ∀ v ∈ ball (0 : Euclid n) s, tangentSpace ((fun v => z + ι v + ι' (u v)) '' ball (0 : Euclid n) s) (z + ι v + ι' (u v)) = (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ (fun v => z + ι v + ι' (u v)) v : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid (n + k)) : Set (Euclid (n + k)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 3, 5 and 6 of the parent proof. Deviation (simplification): the parent used the smaller graph Σ' = Φ(B_{s/2}(0)) with chart target C'; here the whole graph Σ = Φ(B_s(0)) is used with chart target W = Pr⁻¹(D), which needs no bound on u; and the facts (i), (ii) established in the parent's steps 1 and 3 are recorded in the statement because the parent applies the area formula with them.
Notation used throughout: ℝ^m means Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); e₁, …, eₙ is the standard basis of ℝⁿ; ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} are linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w; ι*, ι'* are their adjoints (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint of the underlying continuous linear maps); D := B_s(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ (open ball); Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v); Σ := Φ(D); Pr(x) := ι*(x − z); DΦ(v) := fderiv ℝ Φ v.
Formalization note: unless this child is split further it is a machine leaf (one theorem appended to the frozen GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean, no new import or helper declaration); all lemmas cited are in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission.
1. Adjoint identities. Since ι is an isometry, ⟨ι*ιv, v'⟩ = ⟨ιv, ιv'⟩ = ⟨v, v'⟩ for all v' (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left, LinearIsometry.inner_map_map), so ι*ι = id; by orthogonality ⟨ι*ι'w, v'⟩ = ⟨ι'w, ιv'⟩ = 0 for all v', so ι*ι' = 0. Consequently Pr(x) = ι*(x − z) is affine and continuous, and Pr(Φ(v)) = ι*ιv + ι*ι'u(v) = v for every v ∈ ℝⁿ. Hence Φ is injective on ℝⁿ, in particular on D — this is (i) — and ‖v − v'‖ = ‖Pr Φ(v) − Pr Φ(v')‖ ≤ ‖Φ(v) − Φ(v')‖. Every x ∈ Σ satisfies Pr x ∈ D and x = Φ(Pr x).
2. Derivative, (ii). D is open and u is C¹ on D, so u is differentiable at every v ∈ D (ContDiffOn.differentiableOn_one (or ContDiffOn.differentiableOn with one_ne_zero), then DifferentiableOn.differentiableAt since D ∈ 𝓝 v). Φ = (constant z) + ι + ι'∘u, so Φ is differentiable at v with fderiv ℝ Φ v = ι + ι'∘Du(v) (HasFDerivAt.const_add, the derivative of a continuous linear map is itself, chain rule HasFDerivAt.comp), and Φ is C¹ on D (sums and compositions of C¹ maps with continuous linear maps, ContDiffOn.add, ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff.comp_contDiffOn). Then ι*∘DΦ(v) = ι*ι + ι*ι'∘Du(v) = id, so DΦ(v) is injective. Also ι*(DΦ(v)a) = a for every a ∈ ℝⁿ.
3. Chart, (iii). Let y ∈ Σ. Take V := D, W := Pr⁻¹(D) = {x : ‖ι*(x − z)‖ < s} and ψ := Φ.
 (a) V is open (isOpen_ball); W is open as the preimage of an open set under the continuous map Pr; y ∈ W because Pr y ∈ D (step 1).
 (b) ContDiffOn ℝ 1 Φ D (step 2; the contract writes the order as the cast of the natural number 1, Nat.cast_one) and InjOn Φ D (step 1).
 (c) Φ(D) = W ∩ Σ: by step 1, Σ ⊆ W, hence W ∩ Σ = Σ = Φ(D).
 (d) Properness: let K ⊆ W be compact. If K = ∅ then D ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = ∅ is compact. Otherwise the continuous function x ↦ ‖Pr x‖ attains its maximum t on K (IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn), and t < s because K ⊆ W. If v ∈ D and Φ(v) ∈ K, then ‖v‖ = ‖Pr Φ(v)‖ ≤ t; conversely the closed ball B̄_t(0) is contained in D. Hence D ∩ Φ⁻¹(K) = B̄_t(0) ∩ Φ⁻¹(K). Since Φ is continuous on B̄_t(0) ⊆ D and K is closed, this set is closed (ContinuousOn.preimage_isClosed_of_isClosed with Metric.isClosed_closedBall) and contained in the compact ball B̄_t(0) (isCompact_closedBall), hence compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset).
 (e) For every v ∈ D, fderiv ℝ Φ v is injective (step 2).
 So every y ∈ Σ has a chart as required by IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 n Σ.
4. tangentSpace Σ (Φ v₀) ⊆ range DΦ(v₀). Let v₀ ∈ D, y := Φ(v₀) and w ∈ tangentSpace Σ y: there is γ : ℝ → ℝ^{n+k}, C¹ on (−1, 1), with γ((−1, 1)) ⊆ Σ, γ(0) = y and HasDerivAt γ w 0. Put c := Pr∘γ. Pr is affine with linear part ι*, so HasDerivAt c (ι*w) 0, and c(0) = Pr y = v₀. For t ∈ (−1, 1) we have γ(t) ∈ Σ, so γ(t) = Φ(c(t)) by step 1. Φ is differentiable at v₀ (step 2), so by the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) HasDerivAt (Φ∘c) (DΦ(v₀)(ι*w)) 0. Since γ = Φ∘c on the neighbourhood (−1, 1) of 0, HasDerivAt γ (DΦ(v₀)(ι*w)) 0 (HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq), and uniqueness of derivatives (HasDerivAt.unique) gives w = DΦ(v₀)(ι*w) ∈ range DΦ(v₀).
5. range DΦ(v₀) ⊆ tangentSpace Σ (Φ v₀). Let a ∈ ℝⁿ. If a = 0, the constant curve γ ≡ y is smooth, maps into Σ, satisfies γ(0) = y and has derivative 0 = DΦ(v₀)0. If a ≠ 0, put c₀ := (s − ‖v₀‖)/(2‖a‖) > 0 and θ(t) := c₀·sin(t/c₀); θ is smooth (Real.contDiff_sin), |θ(t)| ≤ c₀ for all t (Real.abs_sin_le_one), θ(0) = 0 and θ'(0) = cos 0 = 1 (Real.hasDerivAt_sin and the chain rule). The smooth curve κ(t) := v₀ + θ(t)a satisfies ‖κ(t)‖ ≤ ‖v₀‖ + c₀‖a‖ = (s + ‖v₀‖)/2 < s, so κ(ℝ) ⊆ D. Put γ := Φ∘κ. Since Φ is C¹ on D ⊇ κ(ℝ), γ is C¹ on ℝ, in particular on (−1, 1) (ContDiffOn.comp with the smooth κ and MapsTo κ univ D); γ(ℝ) ⊆ Φ(D) = Σ; γ(0) = Φ(v₀) = y; and by the chain rule γ'(0) = DΦ(v₀)(θ'(0)a) = DΦ(v₀)a. Hence DΦ(v₀)a ∈ tangentSpace Σ y. (Sine replaces the parent's tanh only because its smoothness and derivative lemmas are directly available.)
6. Steps 4 and 5 give (iv): tangentSpace Σ (Φ v₀) equals the range of fderiv ℝ Φ v₀ (regarded as a linear map, coerced to a set) for every v₀ ∈ D. Together with steps 1–3 this proves all four conjuncts. ∎

subproblems.title: The graph map does not decrease measure and has locally finite image measure
subproblems.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0, s > 0, z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k of class C¹ on D = B_s(0), and Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v). Then (i) for every Borel A ⊆ D and every Borel g : ℝ^{n+k} → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_A g(Φ(v)) dv ≤ ∫⁻_{Φ(A)} g dHⁿ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]); and (ii) for every t < s, Hⁿ(Φ(B̄_t(0))) < ∞.

Source: step 8 of the parent proof (consequences (a) and (b) of the area formula). Deviation (simplification): (i) is proved from the 1-Lipschitz projection Pr instead of the area formula, and (ii) by the Lipschitz bound, exactly as in the parent's 8(b); neither needs the nonlinear area formula.
Notation used throughout: ℝ^m means Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); Hⁿ := μHE[n] (on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n); ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} are linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w; ι* is the adjoint of ι; D := B_s(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ (open ball); Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v); Pr(x) := ι*(x − z); DΦ(v) := fderiv ℝ Φ v.

Since ι is an isometry, ⟨ι*ιv, v'⟩ = ⟨ιv, ιv'⟩ = ⟨v, v'⟩ for all v' (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left, LinearIsometry.inner_map_map), so ι*ι = id; by orthogonality ⟨ι*ι'w, v'⟩ = ⟨ι'w, ιv'⟩ = 0 for all v', so ι*ι' = 0. 2. Two facts on Hausdorff measure. (a) Hⁿ on ℝⁿ is Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n), as measures and hence also on non-measurable sets. 6. Part (ii). If t < 0 then B̄_t(0) = ∅ and Hⁿ(Φ(∅)) = 0 ≠ ∞. Let 0 ≤ t < s and K := B̄_t(0), a compact convex subset of D. Since Φ is C¹ on the open set D, v ↦ DΦ(v) is continuous on D (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen), hence bounded on K by some Λ ≥ 0 (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn; take the bound in ℝ≥0, e.g. Λ := C.toNNReal). By step 2, Hⁿ(Φ(K)) ≤ Λⁿ·Hⁿ(K) = Λⁿ·Lⁿ(K) < ∞ (compact sets have finite Lebesgue measure). ∎
proof_key_steps: Pr := ι*(· − z) is 1-Lipschitz with Pr∘Φ = id, so Lⁿ(S) = Hⁿ(Pr(Φ(S))) ≤ Hⁿ(Φ(S)) for all S ⊆ ℝⁿ.
Hence Φ_#(Lⁿ⌞A) ≤ Hⁿ⌞Φ(A) for Borel A ⊆ D (only A and the test set S need be measurable), giving the lower-integral inequality.
On B̄_t(0) (t < s) Φ is Lipschitz by the mean value inequality, so Hⁿ(Φ(B̄_t(0))) < ∞.

subproblems.title: Continuous unit orientation of a C¹ graph and the Jacobian identity for n-covectors
subproblems.statement: Let n ≥ 1, k ≥ 0, ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w, s > 0, z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k of class C¹ on the open ball D = B_s(0), Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v), Σ := Φ(D), b(v) := (DΦ(v)e₁, …, DΦ(v)eₙ) with DΦ(v) = fderiv ℝ Φ v, and J(v) := √det(DΦ(v)*∘DΦ(v)) (DΦ(v)* the adjoint). Then there exist ξ : ℝ^{n+k} → Λₙ(ℝ^{n+k}) (the contract's MultiVector (n+k) n, continuous linear functionals on n-covectors) and β : ℝ^{n+k} → Λⁿ(ℝ^{n+k}) (n-covectors), both continuous on Σ, such that (a) ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 for every x ∈ Σ; (b) for every v ∈ D, ξ(Φ(v)) is a unit orientation of the subspace range DΦ(v) (IsUnitOrientationOf); (c) for every v ∈ D and every n-covector α, α(b(v)) = J(v)·ξ(Φ(v))(α).

subproblems.natural_proof:

Notation used throughout: ℝ^m means Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m); e₁, …, eₙ is the standard basis of ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.single i 1); ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} are linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w; ι* is the adjoint of ι; D := B_s(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ (open ball); Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v); Σ := Φ(D); Pr(x) := ι*(x − z); F(v) := DΦ(v) := fderiv ℝ Φ v; bᵢ(v) := F(v)eᵢ and b(v) := (b₁(v), …, bₙ(v)); A(v) := F(v)*∘F(v), i.e. (fderiv ℝ Φ v).adjoint ∘L fderiv ℝ Φ v, an endomorphism of ℝⁿ; J(v) := √(det A(v)) (ContinuousLinearMap.det, Real.sqrt). "n-covector" means an element of Covector (Euclid (n+k)) n (a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^{n+k} → ℝ); MultiVector (n+k) n is the space of continuous linear functionals on n-covectors.
Formalization note: unless this child is split further it is a machine leaf (one theorem appended to the frozen GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean, no new import or helper declaration); all lemmas cited are in the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission.
1. Adjoint identities. Since ι is an isometry, ⟨ι*ιv, v'⟩ = ⟨ιv, ιv'⟩ = ⟨v, v'⟩ for all v' (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left, LinearIsometry.inner_map_map), so ι*ι = id; by orthogonality ⟨ι*ι'w, v'⟩ = ⟨ι'w, ιv'⟩ = 0, so ι*ι' = 0. Hence Pr(Φ(v)) = ι*ιv + ι*ι'u(v) = v for every v ∈ ℝⁿ, and Pr is continuous (affine).
2. Derivative. D is open and u is C¹ on D, so u is differentiable at every v ∈ D and F(v) = ι + ι'∘Du(v) (derivative of z + ι(·) + ι'(u(·)), chain rule). Therefore ι*∘F(v) = id + ι*ι'∘Du(v) = id; so F(v) is injective, ι*bᵢ(v) = eᵢ for every i, and L_v := range F(v) has dimension n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj). The map v ↦ F(v) is continuous on D (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen, 1 ≤ 1).
3. Linear algebra at a fixed v ∈ D. Write L := L_v and bⱼ := bⱼ(v). Since F(v) is injective and e is a basis, b = (b₁, …, bₙ) is a linearly independent family of n vectors in the n-dimensional space L, hence a basis of L. Choose an orthonormal basis τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) of L indexed by Fin n (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ L reindexed along finrank L = n; regard τᵢ ∈ ℝ^{n+k}). Since bⱼ ∈ L, bⱼ = Σᵢ 𝒜ᵢⱼτᵢ with 𝒜ᵢⱼ := ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩ (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr, repr_apply_apply); 𝒜 is the change-of-basis matrix τ.toBasis.toMatrix b, and det 𝒜 = det_τ(b) ≠ 0 because b is a basis: with the basis 𝔟 := (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.map (LinearEquiv.ofInjective F(v) (injectivity)) of L (whose vectors are the bⱼ), (τ.toBasis.isUnit_det 𝔟).ne_zero.
 (i) For every n-covector α, α(b) = det(𝒜)·α(τ). Indeed the restriction α_L(c₁, …, cₙ) := α(c₁, …, cₙ) (cᵢ ∈ L; α composed with the inclusion L → ℝ^{n+k} in every slot) is an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space L, so α_L = α_L(τ)·det_τ (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det for the basis τ of L); evaluating at (b₁, …, bₙ) ∈ Lⁿ gives α(b) = α(τ)·det_τ(b) and det_τ(b) = det(τ.toMatrix b) = det 𝒜 (Module.Basis.det_apply).
 (ii) Since τ is an orthonormal basis of L and bᵢ, bⱼ ∈ L, ⟨bᵢ, bⱼ⟩ = Σ_l ⟨τ_l, bᵢ⟩⟨τ_l, bⱼ⟩ = Σ_l 𝒜_{li}𝒜_{lj} (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner), i.e. the Gram matrix Γ := (⟨bᵢ, bⱼ⟩)ᵢⱼ equals 𝒜ᵀ𝒜, so det Γ = (det 𝒜)² (Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose).
 (iii) The matrix of A(v) in the standard orthonormal basis of ℝⁿ has entries ⟨eᵢ, A(v)eⱼ⟩ = ⟨F(v)eᵢ, F(v)eⱼ⟩ = ⟨bᵢ, bⱼ⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right), so det A(v) = det Γ (unfold ContinuousLinearMap.det, then LinearMap.det_toMatrix with (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis, LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right, EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left). Hence det A(v) = (det 𝒜)² > 0, J(v) = √(det A(v)) = |det 𝒜| > 0.
4. Continuity of J. v ↦ A(v) is continuous on D (v ↦ F(v) is continuous, the adjoint is a linear isometric equivalence, and composition of continuous linear maps is jointly continuous), det is continuous (ContinuousLinearMap.continuous_det), and √ is continuous; so J is continuous and positive on D (step 3(iii)), and J⁻¹ is continuous on D.
5. Definitions. Let ev(c) ∈ MultiVector (n+k) n be evaluation at a family c ∈ (ℝ^{n+k})ⁿ, ev(c)(α) := α(c) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid (n+k)) ℝ c, or LinearMap.mkContinuous with the bound |α(c)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏ᵢ‖cᵢ‖ from ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). The map c ↦ ev(c) is continuous: by ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_image_sub_le, |α(c) − α(c')| ≤ ‖α‖·n·max(‖c‖, ‖c'‖)^{n−1}·‖c − c'‖ for every α, so ‖ev(c) − ev(c')‖ ≤ n·max(‖c‖, ‖c'‖)^{n−1}·‖c − c'‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound). Define ξ(x) := J(Pr x)⁻¹·ev(b(Pr x)) if Pr x ∈ D and ξ(x) := 0 otherwise. Let δ be the standard determinant n-form on ℝⁿ, δ(c₁, …, cₙ) := det of the matrix with columns cⱼ, i.e. the basis determinant (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis.det made into a continuous alternating map: e.g. AlternatingMap.mkContinuous with the Leibniz bound |δ(c)| ≤ (card of the permutation group)·∏ⱼ‖cⱼ‖ (|cᵢⱼ| ≤ ‖cⱼ‖), or the volume form of the standard orientation, o.volumeForm.mkContinuous 1 with Orientation.abs_volumeForm_apply_le, or directly continuity of c ↦ det(basis matrix of c) via Continuous.matrix_det (automatic continuity of multilinear maps on finite-dimensional spaces, MultilinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional, is NOT in the import closure). In every case δ(e₁, …, eₙ) = 1. Let β₀ := δ∘ι* (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap δ ι*), the constant n-covector β₀(w₁, …, wₙ) = δ(ι*w₁, …, ι*wₙ), and β(x) := J(Pr x)·β₀ if Pr x ∈ D, β(x) := 0 otherwise.
6. Continuity on Σ. O := Pr⁻¹(D) is open and contains Σ (Pr Φ(v) = v ∈ D). On O, x ↦ b(Pr x) = (F(Pr x)eᵢ)ᵢ and x ↦ J(Pr x)^{±1} are continuous (steps 2, 4 and continuity of Pr), so ξ = (J∘Pr)⁻¹·(ev∘b∘Pr) and β = (J∘Pr)·β₀ are continuous on O (products of continuous scalar functions with continuous vector-valued functions; ContinuousOn.congr with the defining formulas, which hold on O). Hence ξ and β are ContinuousOn Σ.
7. (a) ξ(x)(β(x)) = 1 on Σ. For x = Φ(v) ∈ Σ we have Pr x = v ∈ D, so, using ι*bᵢ(v) = eᵢ (step 2), ξ(x)(β(x)) = J(v)⁻¹·β(x)(b(v)) = J(v)⁻¹·J(v)·δ(ι*b₁(v), …, ι*bₙ(v)) = δ(e₁, …, eₙ) = 1 (Module.Basis.det_self).
8. (c) The Jacobian identity. For v ∈ D, Pr Φ(v) = v ∈ D, so J(v)·ξ(Φ(v))(α) = J(v)·J(v)⁻¹·α(b(v)) = α(b(v)) for every n-covector α (J(v) > 0). This is the frozen conclusion α(fun i => fderiv ℝ Φ v (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) = √(det((fderiv ℝ Φ v).adjoint ∘L fderiv ℝ Φ v))·ξ(Φ v)(α).
9. (b) Unit orientation. Fix v ∈ D, with L, τ, 𝒜 as in step 3. Put σ := det(𝒜)/J(v) ∈ {1, −1} (step 3(iii)). By step 3(i), ξ(Φ(v))(α) = J(v)⁻¹·α(b(v)) = σ·α(τ) for every α. τ is an orthonormal family in ℝ^{n+k} (inner products in L are those of ℝ^{n+k}) with span(range τ) = L = range F(v). Hence IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(Φ(v))) (range F(v)) holds, with the first disjunct (∀ α, ξ(Φ v)(α) = α(τ)) if σ = 1 and the second (∀ α, ξ(Φ v)(α) = −α(τ)) if σ = −1.
Steps 6–9 give the five conjuncts of the statement (continuity of ξ and of β on Σ, (a), (b), (c)). ∎
proof_key_steps: DΦ(v) = ι + ι'∘Du(v) is injective with ι*∘DΦ(v) = id and depends continuously on v ∈ D.
At each v: b(v) is a basis of L = range DΦ(v); with an orthonormal basis τ of L and 𝒜 = coordinates of b, α(b) = det(𝒜)·α(τ) and det(DΦ*DΦ) = det Gram(b) = (det 𝒜)² > 0.
J := √det(DΦ*DΦ) is continuous and positive on D; define ξ(x) := J(Pr x)⁻¹·ev(b(Pr x)) and β(x) := J(Pr x)·(δ∘ι*) on Pr⁻¹(D).
ξ and β are continuous on Pr⁻¹(D) ⊇ Σ; ξ(β) = δ(ι*b) = δ(e) = 1 on Σ.
J(v)·ξ(Φ v)(α) = α(b(v)) by definition, and ξ(Φ v) = (det 𝒜/J)·(α ↦ α(τ)) = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) is a unit orientation of range DΦ(v).

subproblems.title: An approximate tangent plane of a set lying a.e. in a C¹ graph is the graph's tangent plane
subproblems.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{n+k} and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^{n+k} linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0, s ∈ ℝ, z ∈ ℝ^{n+k}, u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^k of class C¹ on D = B_s(0), Φ(v) := z + ιv + ι'u(v), Σ := Φ(D). 1. Adjoint identities. Since ι is an isometry, ⟨ι*ιv, v'⟩ = ⟨ιv, ιv'⟩ = ⟨v, v'⟩ for all v' (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left, LinearIsometry.inner_map_map), so ι*ι = id; by orthogonality ι*ι' = 0. Moreover ‖ι*‖ = ‖ι‖ ≤ 1 (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint.norm_map and LinearIsometry.norm_toContinuousLinearMap_le). Consequently Pr(Φ(v)) = v for every v ∈ ℝⁿ and ‖v − v'‖ = ‖Pr Φ(v) − Pr Φ(v')‖ ≤ ‖Φ(v) − Φ(v')‖. Since v₀ ∈ D and D is open, u is differentiable at v₀ (C¹ on the open set D ∋ v₀), so Φ is differentiable at v₀ with derivative F := DΦ(v₀) = ι + ι'∘Du(v₀), and ι*F = id; hence F is injective and L := range F is an n-dimensional subspace (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj), closed because it is finite-dimensional (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional).

3. Suppose, for contradiction, that y ∈ Q and y ∉ L. Put ε := infDist(y, L) > 0 (L is closed, nonempty since 0 ∈ L, and y ∉ L; IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos), R := ‖y‖ + ε, and f(w) := max(0, ε/2 − ‖w − y‖). f is continuous, f ≥ 0, f = 0 outside the compact ball B̄_{ε/2}(y) (so f defines an element of C_c(ℝ^{n+k}, ℝ)), and f ≥ ε/4 on B_{ε/4}(y). Every w ∈ B̄_{ε/2}(y) satisfies ‖w‖ < R and infDist(w, L) ≥ infDist(y, L) − ‖w − y‖ ≥ ε/2 (Metric.infDist_le_infDist_add_dist).
4. Differentiability of Φ at v₀ (HasFDerivAt, little-o estimate) gives ρ > 0 such that ‖Φ(v) − Φ(v₀) − F(v − v₀)‖ ≤ (ε/(4R))·‖v − v₀‖ whenever ‖v − v₀‖ < ρ.
5. Fix λ with 0 < λ < min(ρ, r)/R and let η(x) := λ⁻¹(x − x₀) (= blowUpMap x₀ λ x), where x₀ := Φ(v₀). Let N := (A ∩ B_r(x₀)) ∖ Σ, so Hⁿ(N) = 0 by hypothesis. Claim: η(A) ∩ B̄_{ε/2}(y) ⊆ η(N). Let w = η(a) ∈ B̄_{ε/2}(y) with a ∈ A. Then ‖a − x₀‖ = λ‖w‖ < λR < r, so a ∈ A ∩ B_r(x₀). If a ∈ Σ, say a = Φ(v) with v ∈ D, then ‖v − v₀‖ ≤ ‖Φ(v) − Φ(v₀)‖ = ‖a − x₀‖ < λR < ρ (step 1), hence ‖w − F((v − v₀)/λ)‖ = λ⁻¹‖Φ(v) − Φ(v₀) − F(v − v₀)‖ ≤ λ⁻¹(ε/(4R))‖v − v₀‖ < ε/4; since F((v − v₀)/λ) ∈ L this gives infDist(w, L) < ε/4, contradicting step 3. So a ∉ Σ, a ∈ N and w ∈ η(N).

Since f = 0 off B̄_{ε/2}(y), (Hⁿ⌞η(A))({f ≠ 0}) ≤ (Hⁿ⌞η(A))(B̄_{ε/2}(y)) = Hⁿ(η(A) ∩ B̄_{ε/2}(y)) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply with the measurable ball; η(A) need not be measurable), so f = 0 Hⁿ⌞η(A)-a.e. and ∫_{η(A)} f dHⁿ = 0 (integral_eq_zero_of_ae), for every λ ∈ (0, min(ρ, r)/R).
7. By the hypothesis HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x₀ Q applied to f, ∫_{blowUpMap x₀ λ '' A} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as λ → 0⁺. The function λ ↦ ∫_{blowUpMap x₀ λ '' A} f dHⁿ is eventually 0 on 𝓝[>] 0 (step 6), so by uniqueness of limits (tendsto_nhds_unique with Tendsto.congr') ∫_Q f dHⁿ = 0.
8. On the other hand, Hⁿ⌞Q is finite on compact sets and has support Q, because dim Q = n (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule and support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule). Since y ∈ Q, (Hⁿ⌞Q)(B_{ε/4}(y)) > 0 (Measure.mem_support_iff_forall / measure of an open neighbourhood of a support point is positive); f is continuous with compact support (hence Hⁿ⌞Q-integrable), f ≥ 0 and f > 0 on B_{ε/4}(y) ⊆ {f > 0}, so ∫_Q f dHⁿ > 0 (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg). This contradicts step 7.
9. Hence Q ≤ L, and as dim Q = n = dim L, Q = L = range DΦ(v₀). ∎

Assume y ∈ Q ∖ L and test with f = max(0, ε/2 − ‖· − y‖), ε = infDist(y, L).

1. Unfolding the hypotheses (IsUnitOrientationOf): there are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q = span(range τ') and signs ε, ε' ∈ {1, −1} with ξ₁(α) = ε·α(τ) and ξ₂(α) = ε'·α(τ') for every n-covector α.

Since τ is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent) and spans Q, it is a basis 𝔟 of Q indexed by Fin n (Module.Basis.mk, or OrthonormalBasis.mk), and dim Q = n; likewise τ' is an orthonormal (hence linearly independent) family of n vectors in the n-dimensional space Q, so it spans Q and is a basis 𝔟' of Q.

Both bases are orthonormal, so this matrix O (O_{ij} = ⟨τᵢ, τ'ⱼ⟩) is orthogonal (OᵀO = I because ⟨τ'ⱼ, τ'_l⟩ = Σᵢ O_{ij}O_{il}) and d = det O ∈ {1, −1} (d² = det(OᵀO) = 1; or OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real).
4. Let α be an n-covector and α_Q its restriction to Q (α composed with the inclusion Q → ℝ^P in each slot), an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q. Every such form is a multiple of det_𝔟: α_Q = α_Q(𝔟)·det_𝔟 (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at 𝔟' gives α(τ') = α_Q(𝔟') = α_Q(𝔟)·det_𝔟(𝔟') = d·α(τ). The number d does not depend on α.

By extensionality of continuous linear maps (ContinuousLinearMap.ext), ξ₂ = ξ₁ if s = 1 and ξ₂ = −ξ₁ if s = −1. For n = 0 the same argument applies (τ = τ' is the empty family, Q = {0}, d = 1). ∎

The change-of-basis matrix is orthogonal, so d = ±1 and ξ₂ = (εε'd)·ξ₁ = ±ξ₁.

Therefore C = {x : ‖Pr x‖ < s and ‖Q x‖ < h} = Pr⁻¹(B_s(0)) ∩ Q⁻¹(B_h(0)), which is open because Pr and Q are continuous (affine). Also Pr∘Φ = id, so Φ is injective.

For Borel S, μ(S) = ∫⁻_{S} θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) = ∫⁻_{M∩S} θ dHⁿ ≥ Hⁿ(M ∩ S) (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict; θ ≥ 1 on M by R.mult_pos, θ being ℕ-valued). With S := (spt μ)ᶜ (open): Hⁿ(M ∖ spt μ) = 0. Since spt μ ∩ C = Σ, (M ∩ C) ∖ Σ ⊆ M ∖ spt μ, hence Hⁿ((M ∩ C) ∖ Σ) = 0. (*)

By R.orients and ae_restrict_iff' (M is measurable, R.measurableSet_carrier), the set N₁ of x ∈ M for which there is no subspace Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_R(x)) Q_x satisfies Hⁿ(N₁) = 0. Then: (a) θ(x)·ξ_R(x)(ω) = g(x)·ξ(x)(ω) for every x ∈ Y and every n-covector ω, by (**) (g(x) = θ(x)ε(x)); (b) g = 0 on Σ ∖ M; (c) for x ∈ Y, g(x) = ±θ(x) ∈ ℤ and |g(x)| = θ(x); hence every x ∈ Σ ∖ N₀ satisfies g(x) ∈ ℤ and |g(x)| ≤ θ(x)·1_M(x) (because Σ ∖ N₀ ⊆ Y ∪ (Σ ∖ M)); (d) g is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞Σ: θ is measurable (R.measurable_mult); ξ_R is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), hence for the smaller measure Hⁿ⌞(Σ ∩ M) (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure with Measure.restrict_mono); β is continuous on the Borel set Σ, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞Σ (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable) and for Hⁿ⌞(Σ ∩ M); the evaluation (ζ, α) ↦ ζ(α) is a continuous bilinear map, so x ↦ θ(x)·ξ_R(x)(β(x)) is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(Σ ∩ M) = (Hⁿ⌞Σ)⌞M; and by aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff (root namespace; M measurable) its indicator g is a.e.-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞Σ (note Measure.restrict_restrict gives (Hⁿ⌞Σ)⌞M = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Σ)).

1. Fix φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C¹ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ D, and fix i. (If n = 0 there is no index i; assume n ≥ 1.) K := tsupport φ is compact and K ⊆ D; choose δ > 0 with K_δ := cthickening δ K ⊆ D (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open); K_δ is compact (IsCompact.cthickening). G is integrable on K_δ (LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_compact_subset with K_δ ⊆ D).
2. Mollifiers. For r > 0 let B_r be a ContDiffBump centred at 0 ∈ ℝⁿ with rIn = r/2 and rOut = r; as a function ℝⁿ → ℝ it is smooth (ContDiffBump.contDiff), 0 ≤ B_r ≤ 1, B_r = 1 on B̄_{r/2}(0), and support B_r = B_r(0) (ContDiffBump.support_eq), so it is continuous with compact support and integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). I_r := ∫ B_r > 0 by integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg, since B_r ≥ 0 and its support, the open ball B_r(0), has positive Lebesgue measure (Metric.measure_ball_pos). Put ϱ_r := I_r⁻¹·B_r. Then ϱ_r is smooth with compact support, ϱ_r ≥ 0, ∫ϱ_r = 1 (integral_smul / integral_const_mul), and support ϱ_r ⊆ B_r(0).
3. For ℓ ∈ ℕ put r_ℓ := δ/(ℓ+1) and φ_ℓ := ϱ_{r_ℓ} ⋆ φ.
 (a) φ_ℓ is smooth: HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left (ϱ_{r_ℓ} smooth with compact support, φ continuous hence locally integrable), with order (⊤ : ℕ∞).
 (b) support φ_ℓ ⊆ support ϱ_{r_ℓ} + support φ ⊆ B_{r_ℓ}(0) + K (MeasureTheory.support_convolution_subset) ⊆ thickening r_ℓ K ⊆ cthickening δ K = K_δ, a closed set; hence tsupport φ_ℓ ⊆ K_δ ⊆ D and φ_ℓ has compact support (closed subset of the compact K_δ; HasCompactSupport.intro).

Given ε > 0 choose r₀ > 0 with |∂ᵢφ(x') − ∂ᵢφ(x)| ≤ ε whenever ‖x' − x‖ < r₀. For ℓ with r_ℓ ≤ r₀ and every x, MeasureTheory.dist_convolution_le (kernel ϱ_{r_ℓ} ≥ 0 pointwise with ∫ϱ_{r_ℓ} = 1 and support in B_{r_ℓ}(0); ∂ᵢφ is AE-strongly measurable; |∂ᵢφ(x') − ∂ᵢφ(x)| ≤ ε for x' ∈ B_{r_ℓ}(x)) gives |∂ᵢφ_ℓ(x) − ∂ᵢφ(x)| ≤ ε for every x.
